mainTopic: How שבועות follows מכות, why its opening משנה lists every 'two that are four' set, what each set means, and whether the משנה fits רבי ישמעאל or רבי עקיבא
overview: The גמרא explains that מסכת שבועות follows מכות, which ended with one prohibition that brings two liabilities, like the edges of the beard. So שבועות opens with a similar pattern: 'two that are four.' The גמרא asks why our משנה lists every 'two that are four' set, while the openings of שבת and נגעים list only their own. The answer is that שבועות and ידיעות הטומאה sit side by side in the תורה and share the קרבן עולה ויורד. Once two sets were listed, the משנה listed them all. The short topic of ידיעות הטומאה is explained first, and the long topic of שבועות comes after. The גמרא then defines each set of four: oaths, awareness of טומאה, carrying on שבת, and shades of נגעים. Next it asks whose view the משנה follows, since רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא each reject liability in one of the lists. It answers that each list includes both liable and exempt cases. The גמרא begins to question that answer, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the quote from מסכת מכות about the beard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה in מכות: the beard has five edges, two on one side, two on the other, and one below.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the beard: two from here, two from there, and one from below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote from the משנה in מכות about the edges of the beard. This quote sets up the next step, which explains how מכות leads into שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in מכות counts how many separate edges of the beard a person can be liable for: five in total. This kind of counting, where one prohibition brings several liabilities, is the link the גמרא will use to explain why שבועות opens with a number pattern.

phrases.english: And for the beard
two from here and two from there
and one from below;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל הַזָּקָן שְׁתַּיִם מִיכָּן וּשְׁתַּיִם מִיכָּן וְאַחַת מִלְּמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote from מסכת מכות that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beard has five edges: two on each side and one below.

steps.title: How מכות leads into 'two that are four'
steps.stepSummary: Because מכות ended with a case of one prohibition carrying two liabilities, the תנא opened שבועות with a similar pattern: 'oaths are two that are four.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There is one prohibition for which he is liable twice. So the תנא continued and taught: oaths are two that are four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the link between the two מסכתות. מכות ended with one thing that brings two liabilities, so שבועות begins with a matching pattern: two that turn out to be four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The theme of 'one that is really two' at the end of מכות flows naturally into 'two that are really four' at the start of שבועות. This explains why our מסכת opens with a counting pattern instead of a plain rule.

keyTerms.meaning: two that are four (two main types that branch into four)

steps.whatToRemember: שבועות opens with 'two that are four' because it continues the counting theme at the end of מכות, where one act can carry more than one liability.

phrases.english: one for which he is liable two;
so he taught: oaths are two that are four.
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of our משנה in שבועות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the connection from the quoted מכות material to the opening of שבועות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא came from מכות, which ended with one prohibition that brings two liabilities. So he continued with 'oaths are two that are four.'

steps.title: Why list every set here but not in שבת and נגעים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה in שבועות lists all the 'two that are four' sets, when the openings of שבת and נגעים list only their own set.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different here, that he teaches all of them? And what is different about carrying out on שבת and the shades of leprous marks, where he does not teach all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a difference in style between מסכתות and asks to explain it. It is a question about how the משנה is arranged, not a challenge to a law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists four sets: oaths, awareness of טומאה, carrying out on שבת, and shades of נגעים. But the first משנה of שבת lists only יציאות שבת, and the first משנה of נגעים lists only מראות נגעים. So why does שבועות gather them all?

keyTerms.meaning: acts of carrying out on שבת (the start of מסכת שבת)
shades of leprous marks (the start of מסכת נגעים)

phrases.english: What is different here
that he teaches all of them,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all four 'two that are four' sets listed in our משנה.

phrases.english: and what is different regarding
carrying out on שבת and the shades of leprous marks,
where he does not teach all of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָכָא דְּתָנֵי לְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained why שבועות opens with 'two that are four,' the גמרא now asks why it lists every such set.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the opening משנה of שבועות list all the 'two that are four' sets, when the openings of שבת and נגעים list only their own?

steps.title: Oaths and טומאה belong together, and the rest came along
steps.stepSummary: שבועות and ידיעות הטומאה are written next to each other and both bring a קרבן עולה ויורד, so they are taught together. Once two sets were listed, the משנה listed them all.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: oaths and awareness of טומאה are written next to each other, and they are alike in the sliding-scale offering, so he teaches them together. And since he taught two, he taught all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step. It gives a special reason why two of the sets belong together in שבועות, and says the others were added once the list had started.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא ה:ב-ד, the פסוקים about טומאת מקדש וקדשיו and about oaths come one after another, and both bring a קרבן עולה ויורד. That shared link is why both appear in שבועות. Once the משנה was already listing two sets, it went on and listed all four. שבת and נגעים have no such link, so each lists only its own set.

keyTerms.meaning: awareness of טומאה (being טמא in the מקדש or with קדשים, and the knowing and forgetting involved)
sliding-scale offering, which goes up or down based on how much the person can afford

steps.whatToRemember: שבועות and ידיעות הטומאה are linked: they sit side by side in the תורה and share the קרבן עולה ויורד. The other sets appear here only because once two were listed, the משנה listed them all.
steps.confusionAlert: Carrying out on שבת and the shades of נגעים have nothing to do with oaths. They are listed here only because the list had already begun, not because they share a law with שבועות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why מסכת שבועות discusses טומאת מקדש וקדשיו at length, even though that topic is not about oaths.

phrases.english: They say: oaths and awareness of impurity
which are written next to each other,
and are similar to each other
in the sliding-scale offering,
he teaches them next to each other;
and since he taught two,
he taught all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: שְׁבוּעוֹת וִידִיעוֹת הַטּוּמְאָה דְּגַבֵּי הֲדָדֵי כְּתִיבָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Oaths and awareness of טומאה are written next to each other and share the קרבן עולה ויורד, so they are taught together. Once two sets were listed, all four were included.

steps.title: The tractate opens with oaths but explains impurity first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a puzzle. The מסכת is named for and opens with שבועות, yet its first chapters explain ידיעות הטומאה instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה opens by mentioning oaths, but then it goes on to explain the cases of awareness of impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the order of the מסכת. Why does it start with שבועות but then explain ידיעות הטומאה first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening line mentions שבועות first, so we would expect the explanations to start with שבועות. Instead, the first chapters deal with ידיעות הטומאה, and שבועות only comes back later. The גמרא challenges this order.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened with (the תנא began with)
Cases of awareness (and forgetting) of one's impurity

phrases.english: He opened with oaths,
yet he explains awareness of impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 4 explained why the two topics are taught together. This step questions the order in which they are explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of topics in מסכת שבועות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מסכת should explain first the topic it opened with. Here the second-listed topic is explained first.

steps.title: Short topic first, then the long one
steps.stepSummary: Because ידיעות הטומאה has few details, the תנא finishes it quickly first. Then he goes back to teach שבועות, which has many details.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the laws of impurity awareness are few, he dealt with them and got them out of the way. Then he went back and taught oaths, which have many details.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: finish the short topic first, then go on to the long one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of explanation does not follow the order of the opening line. It follows how much material each topic has: the תנא finishes the short topic of ידיעות הטומאה first, then goes back to the long discussion of שבועות.

keyTerms.meaning: He dealt with them and finished them off

phrases.english: Since their matters are few,
he dealt with them and got them out of the way;
and afterward he taught oaths,
whose matters are many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about order raised in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Teaching-order principle: the short topic is finished first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The explanations should follow the order of the opening list.
steps.terutzMaskana: The explanations follow how much material each topic has: the short topic is explained first, then the long one.
steps.whatToRemember: ידיעות הטומאה is explained first because it is short; שבועות waits because it has many details.

steps.title: Oaths: two that are four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first set. The two basic oaths are about the future: 'I will eat' and 'I will not eat.' Adding oaths about the past, 'I ate' and 'I did not eat,' makes four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Oaths are two that are four. Two: 'I will eat' and 'I will not eat.' They are four: 'I ate' and 'I did not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list and explains what the 'two that are four' of שבועות are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two' are oaths about a future action, either doing it or not doing it. The 'four' come from adding oaths about the past, which a person can swear falsely. All four are oaths on something he said.

keyTerms.meaning: That I will eat (a future oath)
I ate (an oath about the past)

phrases.english: Oaths: two that are four:
two: 'that I will eat' and 'that I will not eat';
that are four: 'I ate' and 'that I did not eat'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of the מסכת to explaining the משנה's list, item by item.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four oaths are: I will eat, I will not eat, I ate, I did not eat.

steps.title: Awareness of impurity: two that are four
steps.stepSummary: The two basic cases are forgetting one's impurity and then eating holy food, or forgetting it and then entering the מקדש. The other two are knowing about the impurity but forgetting that the food was holy or that the place was the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Awareness of impurity is two that are four. Two: lack of awareness of impurity regarding holy food, and regarding the Temple. They are four: lack of awareness about the holy food itself and about the Temple itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second set in the משנה, the cases of ידיעות הטומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first two cases, the person forgot that he was impure. In the added two cases, he remembered his impurity but forgot what the thing was: that the food was קדשים or that the place was the מקדש.

phrases.english: Awareness of impurity: two that are four:
two: awareness of impurity regarding holy food
and awareness of impurity regarding the Temple;
that are four: holy food and Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four cases: forgetting one's impurity with holy food or with the מקדש, and forgetting the holy food itself or the מקדש itself.

steps.title: Carrying on שבת: two that are four
steps.stepSummary: Using the poor man outside and the homeowner inside, the two basic cases are each of them carrying out. The added two are each of them bringing in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Carrying on שבת is two that are four. Two: carrying out by the poor man and carrying out by the homeowner. They are four: bringing in by the poor man and bringing in by the homeowner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third set in the משנה, the ways of carrying on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'two' are both cases of הוצאה, moving something out from a private domain to a public domain. The 'four' add הכנסה, bringing something in from public to private. Each can be done by either person.

keyTerms.meaning: Ways of carrying from one domain to another on שבת

phrases.english: Carryings out of Shabbat: two that are four:
two: carrying out by the poor man
and carrying out by the homeowner;
that are four: bringing in by the poor man
and bringing in by the homeowner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four acts: carrying out by the poor man, carrying out by the homeowner, bringing in by the poor man, and bringing in by the homeowner.
steps.whatToRemember: In each set, 'two' are the basic cases and 'four' add a parallel pair: oaths about the past, forgetting the object itself, or bringing in.

steps.title: The two shades of leprous marks that are really four
steps.stepSummary: The two main shades of נגעים are שאת and בהרת. Each has a secondary shade, which makes four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shades of leprous marks: there are two that are really four. The two are שאת and בהרת. They become four because each one also has a secondary shade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last example in the משנה's list of 'two that are four': the shades of צרעת marks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier examples. There are two basic items, שאת and בהרת, and each one comes with a related secondary form, so the total is four.

keyTerms.meaning: The shades or colors of צרעת marks on the skin
A white צרעת mark, the shade of clean wool
A bright white צרעת mark, the shade of snow
Its secondary form: a related, lesser shade

steps.whatToRemember: All four lists in the משנה follow one pattern: two basic cases, plus two related cases, for a total of four.

phrases.english: Shades of leprous marks: two that are four.
The two: a se'et and a baheret.
That are four: a se'et and its secondary shade,
phrases.notes: 'Secondary shade' means a similar mark that is a slightly lesser white than the main one.

phrases.english: and a baheret and its secondary shade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the series of explanations of each 'two that are four' in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four shades are שאת, בהרת, and the secondary shade of each.

steps.title: Whose opinion is the משנה? Neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי עקיבא fits
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists oaths about the past and forgetting the מקדש as part of its fours. רבי ישמעאל holds there is no liability for past oaths. רבי עקיבא holds there is no liability for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? It cannot be רבי ישמעאל, and it cannot be רבי עקיבא. רבי ישמעאל says a person is liable only for oaths about the future. רבי עקיבא says a person is liable for forgetting that he is impure, but not for forgetting that the place is the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the משנה, and shows that both likely candidates clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 counted oaths about the past as part of the four, but רבי ישמעאל gives no liability for them. Step 8 counted forgetting the מקדש as part of the four, but רבי עקיבא gives no liability for that. So each תנא disagrees with one of the lists.

keyTerms.meaning: The future: an oath about something that has not happened yet
Forgetting that the place is the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Each תנא clashes with a different list. רבי ישמעאל's problem is the oaths list. רבי עקיבא's problem is the impurity list.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our mishna?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא!
phrases.english: It is neither Rabbi Yishmael nor Rabbi Akiva!
If it is Rabbi Yishmael, doesn't he say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל הֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
phrases.english: One is liable only for oaths about the future.
If it is Rabbi Akiva, doesn't he say:
For forgetting the impurity, one is liable,
but one is not liable for forgetting the מקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לֹא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the lists are explained, the גמרא tests whether they fit any known opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's counting of past oaths and forgetting the מקדש among its fours.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each candidate תנא denies liability in one of the cases the משנה counts, so no one seems to fit the whole משנה.

steps.title: Either תנא works: the four include liable and exempt cases
steps.stepSummary: The משנה can follow רבי ישמעאל or רבי עקיבא. Its list of four simply contains some cases that bring liability and some that are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say it is רבי ישמעאל, or you can say it is רבי עקיבא. If it is רבי ישמעאל, some of the four oaths bring liability and some are exempt. If it is רבי עקיבא, some of the four impurity cases bring liability and some are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה can match either תנא, because the four in each list are not all cases of liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that every item counted in the משנה brings a קרבן. The answer drops that assumption: the משנה only counts the cases, which include both liable and exempt ones. For רבי ישמעאל, the past oaths are the exempt ones. For רבי עקיבא, forgetting the מקדש is the exempt case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces a possible answer
Some of them bring liability and some are exempt

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is Rabbi Yishmael;
if you wish, say it is Rabbi Akiva.
If you wish, say it is Rabbi Yishmael:
some of them are for liability and some of them are for exemption.
phrases.notes: For him, the future oaths bring liability and the past oaths are exempt.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is Rabbi Akiva:
some of them are for liability and some of them are for exemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of whose view the משנה follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the משנה's count means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case the משנה counts brings liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה counts cases, some liable and some exempt, so it fits either תנא.

steps.title: Can the משנה really be listing exempt cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expresses surprise at the idea that the משנה's count includes exempt cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a challenge to the answer it just gave. The full argument continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 12 depended on the משנה listing cases that bring no liability. The גמרא now asks whether that makes sense. The full challenge continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: For exemption: a case that brings no liability

phrases.english: For exemption?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's fours include exempt cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems odd for the משנה to count exempt cases. The full reasoning continues on the next amud.
